newsitem.title: MACAU: China urges Macau to get tough on crime wave.
newsitem.headline: China urges Macau to get tough on crime wave.

text.p: China's de facto mission in Macau urged the territory's Portuguese-run government on Monday to take stronger measures to curb a violent wave of crime that it said was undermining social stability.
In an unusual public move, China's Xinhua News Agency branch faxed statements to the local media asking the Macau government to take "stronger measures" against crime.
Macau, which reverts to Chinese rule in December 1999, has been hit by a series of explosions, murders, muggings, stabbings, robberies and gang-fights since late 1995.

A senior casino police official was the target of an assassination attempt last Tuesday which police believed was ordered by triads, or underworld gangs, infuriated by recent clampdowns on illicit gambling and casino loansharking.
The Xinhua statement said China was strongly opposed to crime and stressed the present crime wave was detrimental to Macau's stability, economic development and the smooth transition to Chinese rule.
